summary: Unexpected 5xx wave during graceful shutdown of ephemeral runtimes causing elevated error rates
description: Issue summary: Between 18:43 and 19:15 UTC on 2026-03-13 we observed a sharp increase in 5xx responses for a subset of tenant traffic in us-east-1. The API gateway returned 502/503/504 to callers and customers reported failed streaming responses and increased latencies. Impact: Multiple dedicated-tier customers (notably CortexAnalytics) saw elevated error rates (~8-12% 5xx for affected routes) and increased end-to-end latency for short chat requests. Environment: prod (us-east-1), dedicated nodes for CortexAnalytics running rw-open-13B-v2. Observed behavior: spikes coincide with an autoscaler drain event on a pool of ephemeral runtimes. Gateways retried requests aggressively during the drain which amplified failures and surfaced as a sustained 5xx wave.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate a rolling scale-down of ephemeral runtime pool with drain timeout configured to 60s
2) Send sustained short chat requests (~50 qps) to tenant routes with keepalive connections enabled
3) Observe gateway retry behavior when downstream returns transient connection errors during drain
4) Measure 5xx rate at api-gateway and track runtime process exit logs during drain
logs: 2026-03-13T18:44:02Z apigw prod us-east-1 route=/v1/chat status=502 backend_error='connection reset by peer' retry=1
2026-03-13T18:44:03Z runtime instance-id=ephemeral-42 drain=started pid=8412 signal=SIGTERM graceful_timeout=60s
2026-03-13T18:44:05Z apigw retry policy: attempts=3 backoff=linear jitter=disabled
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: drain process causing connection resets which the gateway retries without jitter, creating synchronous retry storms.
SRE replicated drain locally: when runtimes hold long-lived keepalive streams, shutdown blocks on in-flight websocket/stream sessions and then force-closes sockets, returning ECONNRESET.
Gateway configuration had a policy of up to 3 retries with no exponential backoff for these tenant routes; retries overlapped with other clients targeting the same draining pool.
No evidence of NVML/GPU driver OOMs or model worker OOMs; observed runtime processes exit cleanly after force-close timeout.
Related runbook: Runtime graceful shutdown (confluence link). We found the runtime did not signal 'draining' to the route health checker early enough, so routing continued until socket closes.
Timeline correlation: autoscaler triggered drain at 18:43:58 UTC, 5xx increase begins within 4s and peaks by 18:46 UTC. Temporary mitigation at 18:52 UTC reduced p50 latency and 5xx rate.
Customer reports: CortexAnalytics support contact (phone + slack) reported errors at 18:50 and provided sample request IDs for tracing.
mitigation: Short-term: applied api-gateway config change to reduce max retries from 3 to 1 for chat routes for 15 minutes and enabled jittered backoff - rolled at 18:52 UTC.
Rerouted new traffic away from draining pool by marking nodes as 'draining' earlier in the control plane to avoid new allocations during shutdown.
Notified CortexAnalytics CS rep and provided temporary guidance: retry with exponential backoff and avoid client-side aggressive retries during window.
resolution: Partial fix deployed 2026-03-14: hotpatch to runtime (PR-4821) implements an immediate 'draining' health state on SIGTERM so router excludes node from new requests within 100ms. Gateway change (PR-9182) adds jitter + reduces default retries for streaming/chat routes. Follow-up: scheduled a full rollout of the runtime change in canary on 2026-03-15 and an audit of retry policies across tenant-specific route configs. Customer-facing remedy: enabled a targeted routing policy for CortexAnalytics to avoid ephemeral pool until upgrade is applied.
next_steps: 1) Monitor 5xx rate and latency for affected routes for 72h post-rollout
2) Expand gateway retry policy audit to other regions and tenant-specific overrides
3) Add unit/integration tests for graceful shutdown behavior covering streaming and short RPCs
4) Postmortem write-up and playbook update scheduled with SRE and Runtime teams (owner: Maya Chen, due 2026-03-20)
comments: 2026-03-13T19:01Z - Luis Romero (SRE): We throttled gateway retries and saw initial drop in 5xx. Moving to mark draining earlier in control plane to prevent new handoffs.

2026-03-13T19:12Z - Maya Chen (Oncall SRE): Confirmed runtime exits are not OOMs; observed long socket CLOSE_WAIT followed by forced kill after 60s. Patching runtime to set health=draining on SIGTERM to stop new connections.
2026-03-13T20:03Z - CS (Asha Patel): Notified CortexAnalytics with temporary workaround. Customer reports error rate decreased to baseline after routing change.
